item.title: Comprehensive ChordPro feature-coverage test song
item.justification: The current test corpus covers features across many focused fixtures, but there is no single test song that exercises all supported language directives and delegate features for a holistic visual completeness review. A consolidated .cho file enables quick inspection across backends and helps confirm that feature interactions render correctly.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: A single .cho test song exists that covers all documented language directives and constructs, with explicit section labels for traceability.
All delegate features (ABC, LilyPond, SVG, Grille, Strum, TextBlock, Program) are exercised with clear, minimal examples and safe defaults.
The test song lives in testing/ with guidance for promotion to t/ after review, per AI-generated test policy.
A visual verification guide exists that lists expected backend outputs and any optional dependencies.

item.title: Delegate system: backend-specific handler and config key dispatch
item.justification:
Delegates currently assume a single rendering path. TextBlock and Strum produce a PDF Xform (XObject), which has no meaning outside a PDF context and breaks HTML5 rendering. ABC received a one-off dirty patch (testing/abc.patch) to produce browser-conformant SVG for HTML output. This is not sustainable: every delegate that needs HTML output requires a bespoke workaround.
Proposed solution: introduce backend-specific config key resolution for delegates. When a backend (e.g. html5) looks up setting "xxx" for a delegate, it first tries delegates.<name>.<backend>.xxx and falls back to delegates.<name>.xxx if the backend-specific key is absent. Handler keys become: delegates.textblock.pdf.handler = txt2xform (existing PDF handler) delegates.textblock.html.handler = txt2html (new HTML handler) This generalizes to all delegate settings (not just handler), giving each backend the ability to override any delegate config key.
The abc.patch workaround in testing/ should be replaced with a proper HTML handler path for the ABC delegate, using the same mechanism.

capabilities.capability: Backend-aware delegate key resolution with deterministic fallback (backend-specific key, then generic key).
HTML/HTML5-safe delegate handlers for TextBlock and Strum, while preserving existing PDF XObject behavior.
ABC HTML output path no longer depends on the testing/abc.patch workaround.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Delegate config resolution supports delegates.<name>.<backend>.<key> with fallback to delegates.<name>.<key>, and is used for handler/type decisions in delegate image elements.
HTML5 rendering of TextBlock and Strum no longer attempts PDF XObject-only handlers; output is rendered inline or as an explicit unsupported placeholder without runtime errors.
PDF delegate rendering for existing delegates remains behavior-compatible with current defaults and regression tests.
ABC HTML output uses a proper configured HTML path and no longer requires testing/abc.patch for browser-conformant SVG.

technical-parameters.constraint: Backward compatibility: existing delegate defaults in chordpro.json must continue to resolve to current behavior for PDF and non-HTML backends.
Schema compatibility: config.schema definitions for built-in delegates (abc, ly, strum, svg, textblock) must validate backend-specific subkeys without weakening required generic fields.
Implementation scope is limited to delegate config lookup/dispatch and delegate modules; no unrelated backend rendering refactors.
technical-parameters.nfr: Delegate key resolution remains O(1) per key lookup and adds no external process invocation in HTML/HTML5 TextBlock/Strum paths.
Regression tests for PDF delegate behavior continue to pass unchanged while new HTML5 delegate tests pass consistently.
A single shared resolver function is used by delegate dispatch points to prevent duplicated backend fallback logic.
technical-parameters.pattern: Introduce a shared delegate setting resolver in parser/dispatch path (Song.pm element construction and asset delegate mapping), then consume resolved handler in backends (including HTML5 delegate execution path).

Implement HTML-focused handlers in delegate modules (TextBlock, Strum, ABC) rather than backend-local ad-hoc transformations, keeping behavior co-located with delegate logic (L-7 consistency across preview/print flows).
Add targeted regression assertions that check presence/absence semantics instead of brittle full-string matches where delegate markup can gain extra classes/attributes (L-8).

security-impact.threat: No direct authentication boundary change; delegate dispatch remains internal render-time logic.
security-impact.mitigation: Mark AUTH as not applicable for this item and keep existing application auth model unchanged.
security-impact.threat: Delegate body text can contain markup-like content; new HTML handlers could introduce injection/XSS if emitted unsafely.
security-impact.mitigation: Ensure txt2html and ABC/Strum HTML paths escape unsafe content and avoid emitting executable script/event-handler attributes.
security-impact.threat: Backend-specific key fallback could resolve to unintended config values if lookup precedence is ambiguous.
security-impact.mitigation: Define strict precedence (backend-specific first, then generic) with tests for positive and fallback cases.
security-impact.threat: No network behavior is introduced by this dispatch refactor.
security-impact.mitigation: Keep NETWORK category non-applicable; no URL fetching or remote calls added.
security-impact.threat: Delegate Program-based execution exists in system; dispatch changes must not broaden external command execution paths.
security-impact.mitigation: Restrict change to handler selection for existing delegates and preserve explicit Program delegate requirements in schema/config.
security-impact.threat: Delegate error output in HTML paths could leak filesystem paths or internal diagnostics into rendered output.
security-impact.mitigation: Keep detailed diagnostics in logs/warnings; emit sanitized user-visible placeholders in HTML when unsupported or failing.

tasks.task: Implement a delegate setting resolver for (delegate-name, backend, key) in the parser/dispatch path, with precedence delegates.<name>.<backend>.<key> then delegates.<name>.<key>.
Apply the resolver where delegate image elements are created in Song.pm (start_of delegate blocks and delegate-typed image assets), resolving at least type/module/handler for the active backend.

Update config schema/defaults (chordpro.json + config.schema) so built-in delegate definitions explicitly support backend-specific handler overrides (pdf/html/html5), while preserving current generic defaults.
Add HTML-capable handler for TextBlock delegate (e.g., txt2html) and configure html/html5 handler mapping so HTML backends never call txt2xform.
Add HTML-capable Strum delegate behavior (native HTML/SVG output or explicit visible unsupported placeholder) and map html/html5 handler accordingly.
Remove dependency on testing/abc.patch by configuring/implementing an ABC html/html5 handler path that emits browser-conformant SVG through normal delegate flow.
Add regression tests for backend-specific dispatch: HTML5 TextBlock/Strum/ABC paths and unchanged PDF behavior; include negative assertions that PDF XObject handlers are not invoked in HTML5.
Document delegate backend override usage in relevant developer docs/comments so new delegates can adopt the same key-dispatch pattern consistently.

test.description: HTML5 backend with TextBlock delegate uses txt2html handler and produces inline HTML content.
test.assertions: No PDF Xform is emitted; TextBlock content appears as HTML in HTML5 output.

test.description: PDF backend with TextBlock delegate continues to use txt2xform handler unchanged.
test.assertions: Existing PDF output for TextBlock is unaffected by the dispatch change.

test.description: HTML5 backend with ABC delegate produces browser-conformant inline SVG without the testing/abc.patch workaround.
test.assertions: ABC SVG validates as browser-conformant; no patch file required.

test.description: Render a song with TextBlock, Strum, and ABC delegates in both HTML5 and PDF backends.
test.assertions: HTML5 output shows inline content for all three; PDF output is unchanged.

entry.note: Planned with backend-aware delegate key resolution, schema/default updates, HTML handler strategy for TextBlock/Strum/ABC, and full AUTH/INPUT/DATA/NETWORK/CRYPTO/ACCESS/DISCLOSURE assessment. No separate ENABLER required.
Assigned to DEV for backend-specific delegate dispatch implementation and regression coverage.

Implemented backend-aware delegate resolution, added HTML handlers for TextBlock/Strum, added ABC html handler alias path, updated delegate config/schema defaults, regenerated Data.pm, and verified with focused tests.

r.observations: Delegate resolution is now backend-aware during Song parsing, so delegate image assets carry backend-specific handler/module/type at creation time while preserving PDF defaults. HTML5 delegate rendering now supports delegate results of type "html", enabling TextBlock and Strum HTML output without attempting PDF XObject handlers. ABC html/html5 handler configuration is implemented via abc2svg_html alias and routed through existing abc2svg engine selection, removing dependency on testing/abc.patch for dispatch.
r.lessons-learned: Backend-specific delegate overrides can be introduced with dotted config keys (e.g. html.handler/html5.handler/pdf.handler) while keeping generic handler defaults for compatibility. When parser-time assets are compared structurally in tests, adding metadata fields such as delegate_type requires explicit expected-structure updates.

item.title: HTML5 diagrams.show:right — vertical stacking layout with direction config option
item.justification:
When html5.diagrams.show is set to "right", chord diagram boxes are placed horizontally adjacent to the song content. This crowds the layout when more than one or two chords are used, as the boxes spill into the song area. A vertical column (boxes stacked below each other) is the natural expectation for a right-side chord panel.
Root cause: .cp-chord-diagrams uses display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap (horizontal row-wrap). When show:right, the diagrams panel is an auto-width grid column so diagrams never wrap and spread horizontally without constraint.
Additionally, a config key (html5.diagrams.direction: vertical|horizontal) should allow users to explicitly choose the arrangement, so that horizontal layout remains accessible for compact songbooks that prefer it.

capabilities.capability: Default vertical stacking for chord diagrams when diagrams.show:right is configured.
New html5.diagrams.direction config key (vertical|horizontal) for user override.

technical-parameters.constraint: CSS change must apply to both standard and paged HTML5 output (paged CSS includes html5/css/chord-diagrams.tt directly via content.tt — see L-5).
Config key lives under html5.diagrams (not pdf.diagrams); lookup follows existing html5_diagrams->{key} pattern in HTML5.pm.

Default direction is "vertical" when show:right; when direction is not set, CSS rule .cp-song-layout-right .cp-chord-diagrams { flex-direction: column } provides the default without requiring a class.
technical-parameters.nfr: Direction class naming follows the existing cp-chord-diagrams-align-{value} pattern already in the codebase.
technical-parameters.pattern: Add CSS class cp-chord-diagrams-direction-vertical / cp-chord-diagrams-direction-horizontal alongside the existing align classes (L-5: fix consistently in chord-diagrams.tt so both standard and paged templates inherit the rule).

Pass diagrams_direction from render_chord_diagrams() to the chord_diagrams template, parallel to existing diagrams_align parameter (L-7: preview mode inherits same CSS so screen and print stay aligned).

tasks.task: In lib/ChordPro/res/templates/html5/chord-diagrams.tt, add the direction class to the cp-chord-diagrams div: [% IF diagrams_direction %] cp-chord-diagrams-direction-[% diagrams_direction | html %][% END %] (Added alongside existing cp-chord-diagrams-align-{value} class.)
Run `make` to regenerate lib/ChordPro/Config/Data.pm from the updated chordpro.json. Verify the new html5.diagrams.direction key appears in the generated Data.pm.

Extend t/86_html5_diagram_pos.t with two new sub-tests: (a) show:right with default config → CSS contains .cp-song-layout-right .cp-chord-diagrams and flex-direction:column rule; no explicit direction class required. (b) show:right with html5.diagrams.direction:"horizontal" → output contains class cp-chord-diagrams-direction-horizontal. Follow the existing run_position_test() helper pattern. Update plan tests => N count.

test.description: HTML5 chord diagram placement with diagrams.show:right — direction default and override.
test.assertions: CSS output contains .cp-song-layout-right .cp-chord-diagrams flex-direction:column rule; when direction:horizontal is set, class cp-chord-diagrams-direction-horizontal is present in HTML.

test.description: Render an HTML5 songbook with diagrams.show:right and 4+ chords. Verify boxes appear in a column in the right panel, not side by side.
test.assertions: Chord boxes stack vertically; song content is not compressed by a wide diagram row.

entry.note: Root cause confirmed: flex-wrap:wrap horizontal default in .cp-chord-diagrams. Fix via CSS default rule + direction class + html5.diagrams.direction config key. Lessons L-5, L-7 applied.
All 6 tasks complete. 16/16 tests pass. No regressions in broader HTML5 suite.

r.observations: chordpro.json has two html5 { } blocks that are merged last-wins; the diagrams key had to be added to the SECOND block (the one with mode:"print") because the second block overwrites the first entirely. cfgboot.pl must be run directly (perl script/cfgboot.pl) to regenerate Data.pm since `make resources` skips it when Data.pm is newer than chordpro.json. The built-in default config sets html5.diagrams.direction:"vertical", so the direction class IS emitted for the default case (not absent as initially expected in the test).
r.lessons-learned: When chordpro.json has duplicate top-level keys (both html5 { } blocks), JSON::Relaxed uses last-wins and the entire value is replaced — not merged. Any new key must go in the LAST occurrence of the duplicate. Run `perl script/cfgboot.pl <json> -o <Data.pm>` directly rather than `make resources` to force-regenerate Data.pm.
